title: Europol urges early action to protect cryptocurrencies and sensitive data from quantum threats
source_used: CoinDesk (full text read, account of the Europol report); Europol page is script-only (HTTP 200, no text)
key_facts: Europol's European Cybercrime Center said in its Quantum Computing and Cryptocurrencies report, published on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026, that cryptocurrency wallets rather than blockchains are the main point of exposure to future quantum attacks.
Quantum computers capable of such attacks do not exist yet, and Europol did not predict when they will.
Europol urged a phased transition now: wallet upgrades, post-quantum cryptography, and coordination among developers, miners, exchanges and users.
Europol said exposed public keys cannot be made safe retroactively.
The report said new post-quantum signature schemes can be 10 to 120 times larger than bitcoin's current ECDSA signatures.
Europol described the most likely outcome as proactive adaptation rather than systemic collapse.
quote_evidence: “Cryptocurrencies will not collapse due to quantum computing,” Europol said.
the European Union’s law enforcement agency said “proactive adaptation, rather than systemic collapse, is the most likely outcome.”
why_it_matters_hint: Official EU police-agency warning that crypto wallets should start a phased move to quantum-resistant security before any attack is possible.
